results.title: Arch install fails with "invalid or corrupted package (PGP signature)"
results.section: Arch install fails with "invalid or corrupted package (PGP signature)"
results.text:
This happens when an earlier Arch install was stopped half-way (for example during "Refreshing package lists") and then started again. Every later try fails the same way until the distro is removed. A fix is coming in the next installer release.

1. Remove the Arch distro from the app.
2. Install it again and let the first run finish without closing the app.

results.title: Report a Problem
results.text:
For Linux in the app, Andronix can also send a report by itself when something fails: an install, update or removal that fails, a desktop that doesn't start or stops by itself, Android stopping a desktop, or the app crashing while it runs Linux.

The first time something fails, the app asks **Send problem reports automatically?** and shows what it would send (open **What we'll send** to see the list). When you're signed in, **Linked to your account** links the report to your account; switch it off if you don't want that.

- **Always:** send reports like this automatically from now on.
- **Just this time:** send this one. The app asks again next time.
- **No:** don't send.

You can change it any time in **Settings › Send problem reports automatically**. A report never includes photos or an email address you type, and the same problem is sent at most once a day.

After a report is sent, a notification says **Report sent** with its ID. If we already know the problem, it says so; tap it to see the fix. Offline, it says **Report saved** and sends when you're back online. What a report contains and how long we keep it: see the [Privacy Policy](https://andronix.app/legal/privacy-policy).

results.title: Install in the App
results.text: The app says what went wrong and what to try, for example **Not enough space** or **No connection**, with **Try again** and **Report a problem**. If you're not in the app, a notification says the install didn't finish, with **Try again** and **Send report**. See [Linux in the app: limits and problems](/troubleshooting/in-the-app).

results.title: GPU Acceleration
results.text:
Open **Settings › Linux** and switch on **GPU acceleration** (marked **Experimental**). It applies to every distro in the app, from the next time a desktop starts: stop the desktop and open it again.

The row's caption ends with your device's graphics chip, for example "This device: Adreno 740." It shows the chip whether the switch is on or off, so it doesn't tell you whether acceleration is working.

results.title: The Install Fails or Stops
results.text:
- Every install, remove, backup and restore writes a log to `~/.andronix/logs/` in Termux. Include the latest one when you ask for help.
- With installer 2.0.1 or newer, also include the output of `andronix doctor`: it shows your phone's details and the fixes Andronix applies. See [andronix doctor](/reference/andronix-command#checking-your-phone-andronix-doctor).
- [Report a problem](/troubleshooting/report-a-problem): right after a failed command, run `andronix report` in Termux (installer 2.0.2+), or use the form in the Andronix app. Either attaches your phone's details and gives you a report ID.
- Ask on our [Discord](https://chat.andronix.app), or email [support@andronix.app](mailto:support@andronix.app).
- Check the [FAQ](/troubleshooting/faq).

results.title: Dev Packs
results.text:
In the distro's terminal (Home > **Your Linux** > **Terminal**):

```bash copy
sudo andronix pack add python
```

You can add several packs at once. Andronix checks your free space first, installs the packages in one go, and then checks that the tools actually work. If the check fails, the pack is marked as failed and `pack add` tries again next time.

On Manjaro, `sudo` doesn't work yet: use the root terminal for admin work.

In Termux, name the distro first, for example `andronix pack add debian python node`.
